title: Give dispatch-gates a machine-readable harvest, and a spelling footer
body:
Fixes #13462

Triage ruled the shape at R+50: **形 1 (machine-readable output) as the body, 形 2 (spelling footer) as a mandatory adjunct, 形 3 published only as a transitional measure.** All three are here. `.github/workflows/lint.yml` is untouched — its GATE INVOCATION IDIOM comment is a legitimate idiom and not this card's business.

## The defect, re-derived on current `origin/main` (H2)

The reproduction holds verbatim at `57827b617`, and the four dropped names are unchanged:

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs
total rows: 12   ·   spelled 'pnpm …': 8   ·   spelled 'node scripts/…': 4

dropped by a `pnpm check:` harvest:
  node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs
  node scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs
  node scripts/check-shard-attestation.mjs
  node scripts/check-test-completeness.mjs
```

### ⭐ Sharper than the card measured: the count is not a safe check either

A consumer greping `pnpm check:` over the **whole output** rather than over the block gets **12 rows — the right count and the wrong twelve**. It drops all four direct rows and backfills with three families from the pending-changeset section (which do not apply yet) and one from the unreachable section (which is dead). So a footer printing only `12 families` would have signed that harvest off. **The distribution is what discriminates**: that harvest is 12 pnpm and 0 direct, and the footer says 8 and 4. This is why 形 2 had to be the split rather than a count.

## H1 — the half the card did not accuse still holds

`lint.yml:72-73` claims the direct form loses no discovery. Re-measured at `57827b617`: **all 39** direct-form gate scripts in `lint.yml` are discovered by the derivation, 0 missing. The card's attribution boundary stands — the tool is right, the idiom is right, and the loss is at the seam.

## What landed

- **`--commands`** — stdout carries one runnable command per line and nothing else. **`--json`** — the whole derivation as one document. The banner, the change-set provenance and the new accounting all stay on **stderr**, so a consumer redirecting stdout gets a file it can execute or parse with no filter in front of it. That is the mechanism that makes the hazard structurally unreachable: there is no prose in the stream to pattern-match, so there is no spelling for a pattern to prefer.
- Both modes union the matched families with the **convention-triggered** ones, deduplicated and sorted. Passing both flags refuses (exit 2) rather than silently preferring one.
- **The footer** prints the split on every default run — behind no flag, because it is worthless to an un-migrated consumer if it is hidden behind one.
- **The published harvest.** The correct form was already correct and already in use, as one agent's private discipline stated once in a PR body and enforced by nothing. It is now in the tool's own output and its own source.

### What `--commands` deliberately leaves out, out loud

The pending-changeset families are **disclosed** (their own key in `--json`, a named stderr line in `--commands`) and kept out of the runnable list, because they are derived against a path that does not exist yet. The always-runs tail is likewise named on stderr. A quiet omission is the defect this mode was added to fix, and adding a new one inside the fix is how that defect reproduces itself one layer up.

## ⛔ The three non-empty controls

**1 — `--commands` emits 12, not 8.**

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs | wc -l
12
$ ... 2>&1 >/dev/null | head -1
dispatch-gates --commands: 12 command(s) — 8 pnpm, 4 direct node (12 matched by path, 0 by change KIND).
```

**2 — the OLD harvest is still short on the same input.** Kept deliberately: a new mode returning 12 proves nothing on its own if the old one would too.

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs \
    | awk '/^Local gates for this card/{f=1;next} /^$/{if(f)exit} f' | grep -c 'pnpm check:'
8
```

The defect is real, and it is **untouched** for a consumer that has not migrated. `--commands` is what bypasses it.

**3 — the footer does not hardcode "there is always a direct form."** On `CLAUDE.md`, a genuinely pure-pnpm surface:

```
3 families — 3 pnpm, 0 direct node.
```

The `⛔` shortfall line correctly does **not** fire there: with no direct row a one-spelling grep really loses nothing, and a warning that fired anyway would train the reader on a claim the run just measured as false. Both terms still print, at zero. Pinned as a unit case as well as observed live.

## ⭐ The footer could have broken the snippet it publishes — pinned so it cannot

The published harvest ends the block at the **first empty line**. A footer butted against the rows would be swallowed into it and read as more commands — the remedy breaking the transition it exists to cover. `derive` prints the separator first, and the self-test drives the **real `awk` and `sed`** over a **real rendering** and asserts every harvested row is still a runnable command. Measured after the change: the snippet still yields 12, byte-identical to `--commands`.

## `--commands` is strictly better than the snippet, not merely equal

The snippet reads the matched block alone, so it silently drops the **convention-triggered** block printed beneath it. On `packages/spec/scripts/authorable-defaults.test.ts`: snippet 28 rows, `--commands` 32 — the four it drops are `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:type-check-debt`. Pinned end to end.

## H3 — this settles #13511, and #13511 stands

PR #13500 added one file, `.github/workflows/merged-branch-reaper.yml`, and went red on `check:pm-dispatch-gates`. Replicating that exact surface at `57827b617`:

- the derivation returns **17** families (matching #13511's own figure), and `check:pm-dispatch-gates` is **not** among them;
- `lint.yml:649` spells it **`pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`** — the pnpm form.

⇒ A `pnpm check:` harvest would have **kept** that gate had it been derived. It was never in the list to be dropped. **#13500's miss was a derivation gap, not a harvest drop — #13511 is correctly attributed and is not this card.** The two are not folded.

## Verification

All at `a1ac525ab`, exit codes captured **before** any pipe.

Both convention legs for editing a gate script, quoted from their own verdict lines:

```
✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 1014 cases pass.          (check:pm-dispatch-gates, exit 0)
OK  self-test: 51 live row(s), 43 unreachable as spelled, 43 recorded verdict(s)
    — none stale, none missing, none contradicted.    (bare-root-worklist --self-test, exit 0)
```

The self-test moved 976 → 1014 (38 new cases). `bare-root-worklist.mjs` is the tool's only real importer, which is why that leg is owed.

The derived family union for this diff, re-derived on the final commit and run against it — 14 families, all green, plus `check:nul-bytes`:

```
EXIT=0  node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs        EXIT=0  pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs
EXIT=0  node scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs EXIT=0  pnpm check:entry-guard
EXIT=0  node scripts/check-self-test-wired.mjs         EXIT=0  pnpm check:parse-guard
EXIT=0  node scripts/check-shard-attestation.mjs       EXIT=0  pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates
EXIT=3  node scripts/check-test-completeness.mjs       EXIT=0  pnpm check:pnpm-filter-targets
EXIT=0  pnpm check:agent-test-spelling                 EXIT=0  pnpm check:watch-hint-literal
EXIT=0  pnpm check:bash32-floor                        EXIT=0  pnpm check:nul-bytes
EXIT=0  pnpm check:cli-command-ids
```

`check-test-completeness.mjs` exit **3 = NOT MEASURED** — its own output says so, and it is neither red nor green.

Repo-wide ESLint ran in full rather than narrowed: `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 68s`.

### One red, found and fixed, worth recording

`check:pnpm-filter-targets` went red on my first union run — from **my own self-test fixture**. That gate sweeps the whole tree for `pnpm --filter TARGET` and requires a live workspace package; unlike the watch-hint scanner it does **not** mask self-tests, so an invented `@x` in a fixture reddens it from inside this file. The fixture now names a real package and the reason is comments beside it. A fixture is still a literal in the tree.

## Scope

One file, `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — exactly the declared surface, nothing spread. No changeset: the diff is `scripts/pm/**` only and publishes nothing from any package, so `skip-changeset` applies and is applied.
